header: Date/time: 2026-05-28 16:00 PT; Duration: 52m; Recording: yes; Locale: US-PST; Note: AE+SE from Redwood; Prospect evaluating exit from OpenAI/vLLM stack
summary: Discovery call with CinderPath to map out feasibility of exiting their mixed OpenAI + vLLM/TGI stack. Core concerns: eval parity, tokenization mismatches, latency at p99, dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs, and security (SAML/KMS). Agreed to run a small eval with customer prompts and a perf session next week.
topics: Current stack and pain points (OpenAI usage, self-hosted vLLM/TGI)
Model compatibility and eval parity (outputs, tokenization)
Hosting options: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS/HSM, audit logs
Next steps: share eval spreadsheet, scheduling perf run, pricing options
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Martin: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Alex from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Uh this is Samir our solutions engineer. Can you each quick intro?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Hi i'm Priya, CTO at CinderPath, we run analytics infra and we've got an LLM layer that's partly OpenAI and partly self-hosted vLLM/TGI for bursty work.
[00:16] Javier Morales: Javier here, ML eng, i own serving and the inference pipelines.
[00:20] Mei Chen: Mei, infra lead, i look after k8s and the cloud network, cc: VPC, SSO.
[00:25] Alex Martin: Awesome, quick agenda—map current setup, blockers for exit, parity questions, perf expectations, security and next steps. Sound good?
[00:33] Liam O'Connor: Yeah that works.
[00:36] Samir Patel: Quick one — when you say vLLM/TGI, are you running both in prod or is one for experiments?
[00:42] Javier Morales: Both. OpenAI for chat flows, vLLM for batch summarization currently. TGI for some internal evals but we're hitting quantization and kernel issues.
[00:50] Alex Martin: Okay — helpful. Can you share rough numbers? tokens/day, peak qps, p99 SLA?
[00:58] Priya Nair: We're around 15M tokens/day, peak 220 concurrent requests for chat, p99 target 600ms for user-facing chat, batch can be >5s it's ok.
[01:10] Mei Chen: Network's multi-region, data residency EU + US, KMS keys in two regions.
[01:16] Samir Patel: Got it. So biggest drivers are latency and cost predictability?
[01:20] Priya Nair: Yep, cost variability on OpenAI spend is killing us on large prompt cohorts. Also we want control for SOC2 audits.
[01:26] Alex Martin: Totally — Redwood tends to be chosen for that predictable cost via Dedicated or Private deploy. Something to note: parity from OpenAI can be workload dependent—tokenization and model variant differences.
[01:37] Javier Morales: Can you elaborate? we tried swapping a local LLM into the pipeline and the outputs diverged on some prompts, especially code generation and instruction-following.
[01:45] Samir Patel: Sure — there are a few layers: model architecture differences, tokenizer mismatches (sometimes different BPE splits), and decoding defaults. We often capture a small eval suite and run side-by-side to find delta. Also quantization can change probabilities, so we map tolerances.
[01:59] Alex Martin: We have an eval spreadsheet template — i'll share — that tracks exact prompts, seeds, deterministic settings, and output diffs. Link in notes: [eval spreadsheet shared].
[02:06] Priya Nair: Perfect. On infra side, we're concerned about KV cache eviction behaviour in vLLM vs Redwood's runtime — does that map?
[02:14] Samir Patel: Redwood's runtime does continuous prefix caching and we manage KV cache differently per model. There was a minor mis-transcribe in docs sometimes called "KV cash" but it's cache. The important bit is cache isolation per tenant and TTL controls.
[02:26] Mei Chen: How do you handle on-prem or private deploy? we may need an air-gapped option for one regulated customer.
[02:30] Alex Martin: We offer a Private deployment; control plane can be customer-managed. For air-gapped we have an on-prem bundle and KMS/HSM integration. We'll share the compliance pack.
[02:40] Javier Morales: For parity testing — is there a way to run the customer's TGI/vLLM containers directly on Redwood or do we require conversion?
[02:48] Samir Patel: We don't run their exact TGI binary, usually we pull the model artifact and run on Redwood's runtime. For TGI-specific kernels we emulate equivalent ops; sometimes there's a conversion step for tokenizer or special layer naming. That can be automated.
[02:59] Priya Nair: What about function calling and structured output? we heavily use JSON schema enforcement.
[03:06] Alex Martin: Function calling is supported in the API — we map it to structured output; if you have custom schema we can add a validation layer in the pipeline.
[03:12] Liam O'Connor: Any limitations on streaming? we need partial tokens to the client asap.
[03:17] Samir Patel: Streaming is supported and optimized for low-latency. One caveat: batching for cost savings can introduce more latency — you can tune batching windows.
[03:26] Mei Chen: On networking — how does fallback routing work across regions? we need regional failover and data locality.
[03:33] Alex Martin: Smart routing can send requests to regional pools; when capacity is constrained you can fallback to a lower-cost variant or go to a different region per policy. You'll see per-route cost and latency metrics in the console too.
[03:43] Javier Morales: Let's talk numbers — can you match our p99 600ms target for chat with 220 concurrent?
[03:50] Samir Patel: Depends on model family and prompt length. If you run a Llama-2 13B quantized, you might hit p99 ~700–900ms depending on cold cache. With dedicated pools and warm KV cache, we can approach 350–500ms for small prompts. We'll need to run a bench with your exact prompts.
[04:08] Priya Nair: Okay that's useful. Cost-wise — how's hosted vs dedicated compare for our volume?
[04:14] Alex Martin: Hosted is lower friction but variable cost. Dedicated is a reserved capacity model — predictable monthly commit, lower unit cost. We'll give two pricing scenarios after we review your workload.
[04:23] Mei Chen: Security — SSO is SAML, user provisioning via Okta; we also need audit logs and key rotation.
[04:29] Alex Martin: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, audit logs, and KMS integration with customer-managed keys. For HSM-level controls we have add-on packages.
[04:40] Javier Morales: Any gotchas migrating from OpenAI's tokenizer? we had some prompt length surprises.
[04:46] Samir Patel: Prompt length and tokenization differences can change effective context window. We do a tokenization compatibility pass and suggest prompt rewrites or tokenizer mapping. Also watch out for hidden control tokens in system messages.
[04:59] Liam O'Connor: Are there any legal or procurement hurdles you've seen with customers leaving OpenAI?
[05:05] Alex Martin: Often it's contract termination windows and data retention clauses. Also if you're on an enterprise plan with provider credits, procurement will want to map TCO. We'll support procurement with a migration plan and cost modeling.
[05:16] Priya Nair: For the eval, what do you need from us specifically?
[05:20] Samir Patel: Three things: sample prompts (representative chat and batch), a baseline of outputs from OpenAI/TGI for same prompts, and a snapshot of your traffic distribution (seq len, tokens per request).
[05:30] Priya Nair: We can do that, Javier will export.
[05:33] Javier Morales: i'll export logs and a 50-prompt superset.
[05:36] Alex Martin: Great. We'll run side-by-side diffs and annotate where outputs deviate and why.
[05:41] (pause)
[05:45] Mei Chen: On private deploy, what's the upgrade path? we prefer control plane updates to be out-of-band.
[05:51] Samir Patel: For Private, control plane can be customer-managed and upgrades are scheduled. We provide signed bundles. On Dedicated, we handle updates and you get SLAs.
[06:02] Priya Nair: Any references of customers doing similar exit?
[06:06] Alex Martin: Yes, we recently helped a fintech company migrate off a hybrid OpenAI/vLLM set up — we ran a 2-week eval, parity gap was under 2% for core intents after some prompt changes and model selection. We can share a redacted case study.
[06:18] Liam O'Connor: Can we see the observability dashboards? traces, per-token cost?
[06:22] Alex Martin: Yep, console has token-level cost, traces per request and model route dashboards. We'll share a sample read-only link for the demo.
[06:30] Javier Morales: About quantization — we saw non-deterministic behavior when going to 4-bit. Do you recommend per-model quant profiles?
[06:38] Samir Patel: Exactly. We recommend testing 8-bit and 4-bit on eval set; some models tolerate 4-bit with minimal quality loss, others need 8-bit. We'll provide a quantization profile and suggested knobs.
[06:50] Priya Nair: This is good, i'm worried about timeline — we have a procurement window in July. Can you help accelerate?
[06:57] Alex Martin: Yes, if the eval shows parity we can prioritize a pilot and a dedicated quote. We'll commit to a pilot SOW if needed.
[07:05] Mei Chen: One small nit—how do you handle logs and PII? we need redaction controls and retention policies per customer.
[07:12] Samir Patel: We support configurable retention, automatic PII redaction hooks, and you can opt for no logging in Private deployments. We'll include the security doc showing those options.
[07:21] Javier Morales: Are there known incompatibilities with some TGI ops? we've had custom instruction modules.
[07:27] Samir Patel: Sometimes layer naming or custom kernels need small adapter layers. Usually it's conversion step during onboarding, not a blocker.
[07:34] Alex Martin: Quick recap then: Redwood to share eval template, security pack, pricing scenarios; CinderPath to share prompts, logs, and traffic snapshot; schedule perf run week of 6/8. Anything else?
[07:47] Priya Nair: Could you also include an estimated run cost for our 15M tokens/day in the pricing?
[07:52] Alex Martin: Yes we'll include a model-by-model cost projection and an ops-runbook for migration.
[07:58] Liam O'Connor: And can you include notes on how function calling differences are handled?
[08:02] Samir Patel: We'll add a short doc mapping function-calling behavior and JSON schema validation.
[08:08] (crosstalk)
[08:12] Alex Martin: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the links and next steps.
[08:16] Priya Nair: Thanks, bye.
[51:30] (session end)
